content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., post-80+ levels), often overshooting by 5–15% and failing to correct downward.
- Shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (days 20–30), suggesting mean reversion is not adequately modeled.
- Lags in response to recent price drops — forecasts remain high longer than actuals.
- Tends to overreact to recent volatility, especially when history includes rapid declines, leading to exaggerated downward forecasts.
- Underestimates the magnitude of mean reversion after strong upward moves — fails to anticipate price pullback to prior levels.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fails to capture short-term volatility spikes or sudden reversals in the last 5–7 days.
- Inconsistent with historical pattern: when price drops below 65, model often fails to recognize the trend continuation and underestimates further decline.
